chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ibn Fazzal and Al-Hajjal, all together from Tha'laba from Ziyad, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) descended in a barren land, so he said to his companions: 'Bring firewood.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are in a barren land, there is no firewood in it.' He said: 'So let every person bring whatever he is able to bring.' So they brought it until they threw it in front of him, some on top of others. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'This is how the sins accumulate.'

Then he said: 'Beware of the belittled sins, for every thing has a seeker. Indeed, He who seeks it records what they have sent before and their effects, and We have enumerated everything in a Manifest Imam.'

key_terms.إِمامٍ مُبِينٍ: A Manifest Imam (a key Shia concept referring to a divinely appointed guide or the Quran as a guide)
key_terms.طَالِباً: A seeker (referring to God who seeks/records)
key_terms.قَرْعَاءَ: A barren or empty land lacking vegetation

ai.seo_question: How do minor sins accumulate according to the Prophet's teaching in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the cumulative weight of minor sins through the Prophet’s metaphor of gathering scattered firewood in a barren land, emphasizing that no small deed is overlooked. It connects the concept of divine accounting to the Shia doctrine of the 'Imam al-Mubin' (often interpreted as the Quran or the Prophet), reinforcing the idea that every action is meticulously recorded and will manifest its consequences.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal and Al Hajjal, altogether from Sa;alba, from Ziyad who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> descended in a barren land, so he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said to his<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> companions: ‘Bring me<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> some firewood’. So they said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! We are in a barren land, there is no firewood in it’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘So let every person bring in whatever he is able upon’. So they came over until they threw it in front of him<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, on top of each other. So Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘This is how the sins tend to accumulate’.

Then hesaww said: ‘Beware of the belittled ones from the sins, and for every thing there is a seeker. Indeed! And if you were to seek it, Heazwj would [36:12] Write down what they have sent before and its effects, and We have Numbered everything in a Manifest Imam’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal and al-Hajjal all from Tha’labah from Ziyad who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Once the Messenger of Allah stopped, during a journey on a barren land, for rest and asked his companions to collect firewood. The companions said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, we are in a barren land and there is no firewood around here. ’ He said, ‘Let everyone bring whatever he can.’ They collected firewood and placed one piece over the other before him. The Messenger of Allah then said, ‘This is how sins also accumulate.’

Then he said, ‘You must never commit al-Muhaqqarat (see Hadith 1 above) of sins; everything is in demand. You must know that the finder of sins writes them down: “It is We Who bring the dead to life and record the deeds of human beings and their consequences (of continual effects). We keep everything recorded in an illustrious Imam (leader or Book).”’ [36:12]
